A local inference server keeps a language model resident in GPU memory and answers requests from that resident copy. The first request after a model is loaded behaves differently from every request that follows it, because the weights must be moved across the bus before any token can be produced. Benchmarks that ignore this difference report a loading cost as if it were a generation cost, and the resulting throughput figure describes a situation that never occurs in production.

Generation itself splits into two phases with unrelated performance characteristics. During prefill the server processes the entire prompt at once, which saturates the arithmetic units and draws power close to the board limit. During decode the server produces one token at a time, each token depending on the one before it, which leaves most of the arithmetic units idle while the memory subsystem is pushed hard. A configuration that wins on prefill can lose on decode, so a single tokens-per-second number averaged over both phases hides the trade-off rather than measuring it.

Energy behaves differently again. Power drawn during decode is lower than during prefill, but decode lasts longer, and the energy spent on a request is the integral of power over the whole window rather than a peak reading. Two configurations can reach the same latency while spending noticeably different amounts of energy, and the cheaper one is invisible to any benchmark that stops at wall-clock time.

Three constraints limit what such measurements can honestly claim. The first is placement: if part of the model is offloaded to system memory, the measurement describes a hybrid system rather than the GPU under test. The second is telemetry support: consumer boards expose a narrower set of counters than datacenter boards, so an energy figure may come from an integrated power reading rather than a hardware energy counter. The third is scope: a GPU power reading excludes the processor, the memory, the power supply losses, and the cooling, so any cost derived from it is a lower bound on the real cost and must be labelled as such.
